steps.response:
The image displays an axial cross-section of the thorax with high spatial resolution, clearly distinguishing cortical bone (bright white), soft tissue (gray), and air-filled lung parenchyma (black). This appearance is characteristic of Computed Tomography (CT), specifically a lung window setting. It is not a projection radiograph (X-ray) as it shows a slice rather than a superimposed view, nor is it MRI given the signal intensity of the cortical bone.
